events.title: Constantinople Is Dedicated
events.description: Emperor Constantine the Great presided over a dedication ceremony for the ancient city of Byzantium. He renamed it Nova Roma, and it soon became popularly known as Constantinople. It was the new capital of the Roman Empire.
events.significance: The city became the heart of the Byzantine Empire. For over a thousand years it was a center of trade, Christianity and culture bridging Europe and Asia.

events.title: British Prime Minister Spencer Perceval Is Assassinated
events.description: Spencer Perceval was shot in the lobby of the House of Commons by John Bellingham, a merchant with a personal grievance against the government. Perceval died soon afterward.
events.significance: Perceval remains the only British prime minister to have been assassinated.

events.title: Minnesota Becomes the 32nd U.S. State
events.description: Minnesota was admitted to the Union as the 32nd state. Population growth in the territory had paved the way for statehood.
events.significance: Minnesota's admission extended the United States into the upper Midwest, just before the Civil War.

events.title: Israel Joins the United Nations
events.description: Israel was admitted as a member of the United Nations, about a year after it declared independence.
events.significance: Admission to the UN gave the young state wider international recognition.

events.title: Bob Marley Dies in Miami
events.description: Reggae legend Bob Marley died of cancer at a Miami hospital. He had been trying to return home to Jamaica for treatment.
events.significance: Marley carried reggae and messages of unity and resistance to a global audience. His music still has wide influence today.
